meta.problem: Design a hypothesis-triage practice for a small research team of 4-8 people. Premature consensus increases wasted effort. Unfalsifiable claims decrease trust in results. Over-polished ideas prevent honest critique. Every added idea increases review load.

elites.title: Falsifier-Gated Intake Brake
elites.description: Each week the team meets for a falsifier review, and each member can add rough one-page hypotheses with a stated disproof test. Submissions climb as people see the review is quick and low-stakes. When a prediction fails in public, the intake quota is halved until the open critiques are cleared, so the reviewer pile-up never forms and attention is spread evenly across the surviving ideas. Members feel a brief slowdown after a failure, but they end up with a short list of trusted, falsifiable hypotheses.

mechanism.core_mechanism: A failed prediction triggers a temporary halving of the intake quota, which keeps reviewer overload from happening and leaves critique attention evenly spread over a trusted, falsifiable portfolio.

elites.title: Kill-Criterion Gate: Earned Pause Before Experiments
elites.description: When someone pitches an idea, a rotating reader asks what result would refute it, and a vague answer earns a hold stamp that keeps the idea out of the experiment queue. During the hold, the proposer has a protected period to sharpen the claim using rough sketches rather than polished decks, ending in a written kill criterion. Ideas that later meet their pre-agreed kill test are retired without blame, so the shared results ledger stays lean and trusted.

mechanism.core_mechanism: A hold stamp, earned by an unfalsifiable-sounding claim, blocks the rush to launch experiments and gives the idea a protected rough-sketch period in which a kill criterion is written, so only testable ideas reach the queue and failed ones are retired by prior agreement.

At a fixed, time-boxed adversarial session, the team tears down the rough notes. This stops any favored idea from hardening into consensus, clears the agenda slots, and releases backlog entries with their falsification tests attached. The person experiences a short, intense critique window after which only a small cohort of testable, ranked hypotheses moves on to experiments, so review load stays low.

mechanism.core_mechanism: A deadline-bound adversarial teardown of rough ideas suppresses premature consensus around a favorite during the window before polish sets in, which clears the agenda and exposes backlog entries' falsification tests so that a small cohort of testable, ranked hypotheses advances.

admitted.title: Sealed Stakes, Runner-Up Charge
admitted.description: Before the weekly triage meeting, each member privately files a short note with a confidence number, the stake of review hours they would put behind the hypothesis, and one falsifying result. The highest stake gets the single test slot that cycle, but the stake the author is charged is only the runner-up's. Polishing or inflating a claim therefore buys no extra slot probability or discount, and an honest confidence number is the best move. The team ends up with a ledger of calibrated confidences, and every hypothesis arrives with a clear falsifier.

mechanism.core_mechanism: A charge fixed at the runner-up's stake, not the author's own, keeps authors from inflating or polishing claims, so each author's best move is to file an honest confidence number.

admitted.title: Kill-Test Gate: Earn Your Polish
admitted.description: When someone posts a rough one-paragraph claim for hypothesis A, the owner of rival hypothesis B receives a mandatory kill-test request: write down what result would refute B. Until B's owner answers it, B is blocked from producing a polished pitch deck before the Friday review. Team members therefore see only rough, falsifiable claims in the review slot, and the room sorts them into test-now and park tiers.

mechanism.core_mechanism: A rival's rough claim triggers a mandatory refutation request that blocks the competing hypothesis from being polished before review, so critique happens on rough, falsifiable claims and the portfolio stays small.

admitted.title: Rough-Draft Ladder: Early Demotion of Untestable Claims
admitted.description: Every hypothesis enters as a rough one-paragraph draft with a stated refutation test. Teammates probe each draft for falsifiability during a short window before anyone has invested in polishing it. Claims that cannot name a failing observation are moved down a tiered ladder (flag, then pause, then archive), so the author never gets to build a polished deck around an untestable idea. Authors learn that posting rough, testable drafts is the safe and respected move.

mechanism.core_mechanism: A tiered demotion ladder, triggered by teammates' falsifiability probing, stops authors from polishing and championing untestable ideas during the early window, so rough testable drafts become the habit and the shortlist stays lean and trusted.

admitted.title: Sharpen-or-Shelve Gate
admitted.description: Every new idea arrives as a rough one-paragraph pitch. A rotating skeptic flags any claim that lacks a refutable prediction, and that flag automatically freezes scheduling and consensus-building for 48 hours. During the freeze the proposer, with a peer, rewrites the claim as a concrete 'we would be wrong if...' prediction. If no such prediction exists by the end, the idea is shelved in a visible archive without blame. Ideas that pass enter a short backlog, so people feel enthusiasm held back briefly, then see a cleaner and smaller review queue.

mechanism.core_mechanism: A flag on an untestable claim earns a mandatory hold that blocks the rush to consensus and experiment launch, and the pause leaves time to either sharpen the claim into a refutable prediction or shelve it, which keeps the backlog trustworthy and light.
